chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
It is an obligation for the believer upon the believer that he veils upon him seventy major sins.
ai.seo_question: What is the obligation of a believer regarding the sins of another believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the high status of 'satr' (concealment) as a social virtue that preserves the dignity of the believer within the community. While the number 'seventy' is often interpreted as hyperbolic to indicate comprehensiveness, Shia scholars emphasize that this obligation applies even to major sins, provided they are not publicly known, thereby encouraging humility and preventing the spread of scandal. This principle complements the legal concept of 'satr al-'awrah' but extends it to moral and spiritual faults, fostering a supportive environment for spiritual growth.
